correctness.rationale: PASS: Exact majority-spin elimination gives binomial times cosh(beta s/sqrt(mn))^m; direct independent labelled-spin sums verified this at three finite (m,n,beta) configurations. Writing h(t)=t^2/2−log cosh t, the globally valid 0<=h<=t^4/12 bounds reweighting error by beta^4 s^4/(12mn^2). The supplied Hubbard–Stratonovich proof establishes uniform critical-window fourth moments E S_B^4=O_L(n^3), yielding TV <=C_L n/m without a hidden m/n speed requirement. The Stirling entropy expansion gives exp(lambda x^2−x^4/12) at scale n^(3/4); quartic tail bound secures tightness and moments. Conditional independent majority spins give joint normal transverse fluctuations and asymptotic independence; bound on mean/tanh discrepancy is O_R(n^(3/4)/m)→0. Spin-flip symmetry and uniform moments justify variances. Boundaries beta positive for large n; m>=n, fixed lambda/ bounded windows.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Primary full texts Fedele–Contucci 2010 and Fedele 2013 impose a positive-definite or convex interaction matrix and positive limiting class fractions. Kirsch–Toth heterogeneous 2-group papers discuss N^(3/4) critical normalization with nonvanishing class proportions, not singular n/m→0 with a purely cross-coupled indefinite matrix, nor uniform TV reduction O(n/m). Gallo–Contucci 2007 treats bipartite free energy; classical one-species quartic law acknowledged as background. No statement-level coverage identified, but a general singular multi-population approximation remains possible.
residual_risks: Possible broader critical spin-system approximation for rapidly unequal species not found or ruled out.
Kirsch–Toth 2018 full manuscript was not accessible in this execution; abstract not enough to exclude a hidden stronger theorem.
